paper.title: Scaling Agent Learning via Experience Synthesis
paper.central_claim: DreamGym, a unified framework that synthesizes diverse experiences (reasoning-based experience model + replay buffer + reward-entropy curriculum task generator) to enable effective online RL training of LLM agents, matching GRPO/PPO on RL-ready benchmarks with synthetic-only interactions, enabling RL on non-RL-ready WebArena, and giving a sim-to-real warm start.
paper.central_claim_scope: WebShop, ALFWorld, WebArena-Lite; Llama-3.2-3B / Llama-3.1-8B / Qwen-2.5-7B agents; experience model Llama-3.1-8B; one environment per experience model (author limitation).

provenance.notes: actual_model/session_id/receipt_ref null: not exposed to the worker in this run configuration.

evaluated_retained_non_weight_objects: curriculum task pool (feedback-gated, persisted across iterations)
experience replay buffer (simulator memory, appended online and read at every step)
scope_assessment.reasoning: A3 first bullet (weights as both update object and product) is not met: besides the GRPO/PPO weight update, the system rewrites two non-weight artifacts from execution feedback, the task pool by reward-entropy gate and the replay buffer by appended rollouts, and both are read in later iterations and ablated (Table 2). Domain taxonomy also carries Self-Generate the Curriculum (H23, 'simulated experience grounded in replayed trajectories') as an explicit boundary pattern whose harness-level part is load-bearing. Appendix C shows the generation/selection/annotation/agent prompts are static, so no prompt/skill/tool is retained; the only retained non-weight state is data (tasks, trajectories).
scope_assessment.limits: Policy weights are the deployed and measured product; credit is restricted to what bears on the retained pool/buffer.
scope_assessment.flips_to_out_of_scope_if: The controller rules that training-time task pools and simulator memory (data, discarded after training, not reused by any other agent) are not harness components; then A3 bullet 1 applies and this record would be out_of_scope with score null.

signatures.object: Curriculum task pool (non-weight, persisted across training iterations) of the synthetic RL environment; baseline = fixed seed task set
signatures.information: Agent rollout outcomes in the synthetic env (outcome rewards r in {0,1} predicted by the experience model, n rollouts per task); LLM sees seed task text only. No real-env signal, no independent verifier.
signatures.operation: Compute per-task group reward variance V_tau; choose high-variance seed tasks; prompted LLM (shares params with experience model) generates K variations (same action type, changed targets/constraints) and a second prompted LLM call selects the 'most challenging yet feasible' one; add to pool under a synthetic-share cap lambda.
signatures.output: Expanded task set used for next-iteration rollouts.
signatures.conditions: Needs informative synthetic rewards; PPO needs semantic clustering to form groups.
signatures.feedback: Reward variance across agent rollouts inside the simulator (4.2 Eq. 7).
signatures.selection_rule: Variance gate on seeds + LLM selection among K candidates + lambda cap; no rejection log, no retirement of solved/low-variance tasks described.
signatures.selection_data: Synthetic-env rewards on training tasks; not the held-out eval tasks.
signatures.persistence: Task pool grows across iterations until convergence/budget; no versioning, rollback or expiry described.
signatures.later_use: Sampled as training tasks in later iterations; pool not transferred to other agents or reused after training.
signatures.claimed_effect: w/o Task Generation: WebShop 63.9->57.3 (-6.6), WebArena 13.3->7.3 (-6.0); earlier plateau on WebShop curve.
signatures.failure_boundary: Validity/feasibility certified only by prompted LLM + simulator-produced reward variance (generator and certifier coupled); variance may reflect simulator stochasticity; no random-variation or matched-volume untargeted control.

signatures.object: Experience replay buffer (non-weight memory of the experience model); baseline = experience model without retrieval
signatures.information: Seeded with offline real trajectories (WebShop ~3.6K, ALFWorld ~5.2K, WebArena 4.8K trajectories, with teacher-LLM reasoning); appended with synthetic agent-simulator trajectories.
signatures.operation: At each simulated step retrieve top-k similar (state, action) demonstrations by cosine similarity and feed them with task and history to a CoT experience model that predicts next state and reward; append new trajectories online.
signatures.output: Next state and reward for the agent; enriched buffer.
signatures.conditions: Semantic encoder phi unspecified; k unspecified; offline data volume 2K-40K transitions studied (Fig 5).
signatures.feedback: New trajectories produced by the agent-simulator interaction (no external check on their correctness).
signatures.selection_rule: None described for writes (no gate, dedup, expiry, conflict handling); retrieval by similarity only.
signatures.persistence: In-memory growing buffer for the training run; no stated versioning or rollback.
signatures.later_use: Read at every subsequent simulated step.
signatures.failure_boundary: Ablation removes the whole retrieval+buffer so the enrichment/retention part cannot be separated from the seeded offline data; model-generated trajectories enter memory ungated.

signatures.object: Agent policy weights (excluded from retained-component credit)
signatures.claimed_effect: Table 1 success rates; S2R warm start
signatures.failure_boundary: Weight-level gains are the headline numbers but cannot be credited to the non-weight retained components without the component ablations (S1, S2).

gap.author_gap: RL for LLM agents needs costly, low-diversity, reward-unreliable, infrastructure-heavy real-environment rollouts; existing synthetic-data work still needs real-environment collection or only does SFT-style trajectory variation.
gap.checked_gap: Concrete and important for web/GUI agents (WebArena-Lite baselines 4.8-7.3% under an infrastructure-limited pipeline). For the retained non-weight objects the true 'previously fixed' items are the static task set and a static simulator memory; the paper does not frame its gap that way.
gap.lineage: Dreamer/world-model RL -> WebDreamer/WebEvolver (LLM world model for planning/training) -> UI-Simulator (LLM step simulator, SFT) -> DreamGym (RL + replay + reward-entropy curriculum); task-synthesis branch AgentSynth/SCA (real-env dependent); self-evolving curricula for WebArena (WebRL = Qi et al. 2024, cited only for sparse reward / setup).

claims.result_denominator: no estimate of eps_R or eps_P
claims.allowed_conclusion: A conditional bound; not a verified guarantee for these experiments.

assessment.strongest_supported_claim: On three web/embodied benchmarks with fixed held-out test sets, single-run policies trained on DreamGym synthetic rollouts reach roughly real-env RL level on WebShop, 3-9 pts below on ALFWorld, and exceed infrastructure-limited real-env baselines on WebArena-Lite (9.1-14.5 vs 4.8-7.3); removing the replay buffer, reasoning, or task generator lowers success by about 4-8 pts.
assessment.author_claim_preserved: DreamGym, a unified framework that synthesizes diverse experiences (reasoning-based experience model + replay buffer + reward-entropy curriculum task generator) to enable effective online RL training of LLM agents, matching GRPO/PPO on RL-ready benchmarks with synthetic-only interactions, enabling RL on non-RL-ready WebArena, and giving a sim-to-real warm start.
not_supported: total-cost advantage including offline data and teacher annotation
Theorem 1 as a guarantee for reported runs
retained curriculum/buffer entries reused beyond the training run or by another agent
unresolved: Whether WebArena leaderboard demonstrations overlap the 165 Lite eval tasks (E008)
k, lambda, n rollouts, K variations, encoder phi, number of runs/seeds (not reported)

retained_trace.before: static seed task set / retrieval-free simulator
retained_trace.proposed_change: LLM task variations from high-variance seeds; appended trajectories
retained_trace.selection: variance gate + LLM pick among K; no gate on buffer writes
retained_trace.persisted: task pool and replay buffer for the run
retained_trace.measured_gain: Table 2 whole-module ablation deltas (single run); not independent held-out retained transfer

assessment.note: evidence_level=task: gains are on policy weights trained with the artifacts; whole-module ablations do not isolate retained changes and no independent reuse of the retained artifact is shown.

G.reason: Real, stakes-backed limitation (RL on web agents blocked by rollout cost/task scarcity; WebArena-Lite baselines 4.8-7.3%) and UI-Simulator contrasted precisely. Incomplete: nearest neighbors for the curriculum part (WebRL, AgentSynth, SCA) are not compared, the retained-object gap (static task pool/simulator memory) is not articulated, residual bottleneck not isolated.

M.reason: Operation chain is concrete (variance gate -> prompted variations -> LLM selection -> pool; top-k retrieval conditioning CoT simulator) and responds to the stated gap. Weak links: gate and reward come from the simulator itself, no independent validity anchor (S1/S2 unmet), Theorem 1 premises never measured, no distinguishing prediction vs random variation.

X.reason: Main steps and all prompts are disclosed (C.1-C.4) and next-round read-back is real (S3 met, retrieval at each step). Missing: any admission gate/dedup/expiry/versioning/rollback for the buffer or pool, retirement of solved tasks, and key hyperparameters (k, lambda, n, K, encoder).

E.measurement.reason: Real-env fixed-split success metrics are credible and the downstream objective is measured. Offsets: WebArena-Lite n=165 with acknowledged evaluator errors, fidelity measured only by an unvalidated GPT-4o judge that never sees real next states, text headline contradicts Table 1 (>30% vs 9.1-14.5).

E.causality.reason: Relevant component ablations (replay, reasoning, task generation) with 4-8 pt drops. Key controls absent: gate-off or random-variation vs entropy gate, enrichment-off vs seeded static buffer, matched-volume untargeted synthesis; headline vs real RL confounded by expert/teacher data and a 4-session baseline; Table 2 backbone ambiguous.

E.holdout.reason: Explicit fixed test split with training data only from remaining tasks (WebShop) and 165-task Lite eval vs 647 train tasks; curriculum selection uses synthetic rewards not test. Open: leaderboard demonstrations used to build the WebArena experience model may include eval tasks (unreported), no checkpoint-selection protocol, ALFWorld seen/unseen unspecified, no independent reuse of retained artifacts, single-environment scope and ALFWorld transfer drop.

E.statistics.reason: Sample sizes are given (165 tasks, 100 judged trajectories) and negative cells are reported (ALFWorld, cross-domain), but no seeds, CIs or tests for any Table 1/2 cell; Fig 3 bands lack run counts; 1 task = 0.6 pt on WebArena-Lite so several ablation gaps are 6-10 tasks.

E.cost.reason: Wall-clock/GPU-hour advantage is claimed on WebArena (E016) but experience-model SFT, teacher-LLM reasoning annotation, LLM serving, offline expert data and curriculum rollout cost are excluded ('real data 0'), and the real-env baseline is limited to four sessions.

rationale: 边界范围内：被反馈驱动并留存的非权重对象是课程任务池与回放缓冲，但被测产物是RL策略权重。真实留出集上WebShop近RL基线、ALFWorld低3–9点、WebArena-Lite高于受限基线；消融仅整模块单次；缺留存门控、合成奖励保真度未测、成本漏计；证据级task，scoped。
